items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: Quincy, David Foster or any of these things, they would send me a cassette of the song... track, which was basically David Foster, you just write whatever you want to write

ctx.x: So when you got a lead sheet — what did they give you? What did their producer give you and did you pay attention to it?

Almost in every case all I got was, well back then a cassette. You know Quincy, David Foster or any of these things, they would send me a cassette of the song. That’s it. If I ever got a lead sheet –- which was rare — I never looked at it because by the time the lead sheet — I did it in the beginning. Okay the guy sent me the lead sheet, usually just kind of rough chords, and I figured out that okay they repeated that and then they cut out these bars the next time and then they did this the next. You know it was…

You know you pretty much answered a question of mine because I’ve done some of this and I wondered, you seem to be indicating that what was on the cassette was pretty much a finished rhythm track and it had a vocal on it, whether it was just a scratch vocal or something to show you where the singing was.

items.q: Well I don’t know if they, you know, really Quincy may, Foster may, but you know a lot of the other people that are more producers and less musician, you know they’re not necessarily

ctx.x: Do you ever get over the moment of, I don’t know if anxiety is the right word, but the first time you’re reading down what you arranged and you’re in the studio and the producer is there and you’re waiting to hear the comment about your parts — or do they already know sort of what it’s going to sound like?

Well I don’t know if they, you know, really Quincy may, Foster may, but you know a lot of the other people that are more producers and less musician, you know they’re not necessarily, but the reason they hired me was because they liked what I’ve done in the past, so they know, I guess they’re assuming that it’s going to be what they’re looking © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

for. You know sometimes they’ll say, “You know I’m not really sure on that one.” And okay, what can I do to make it better? But anything that I write, I don’t care, it’s their record if they don’t like it I’ll change it.
